alternatives: GaussianNB may outperform random forest if the dataset is small, noisy, or nearly conditionally independent per feature.
Any gain may be due to ensemble variance reduction rather than nonlinear interaction modeling.
candidates.applicability: Applies when the fixed split contains nonlinear feature-label relationships or feature interactions; depth 6 may underfit if interactions require deeper splits.
falsification: Random forest accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split.
Random forest accuracy does not exceed GaussianNB even when nonlinear interactions are present in the fixed split.
candidates.mechanism: Random forest averages 200 depth-6 decision trees trained on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets, approximating nonlinear interactions and reducing variance relative to a single tree.
predictions: On the fixed public split, random_forest with max_depth=6 and n_estimators=200 will achieve higher diagnostic label accuracy than GaussianNB.
The improvement will be larger when relevant features have threshold-like or interaction effects rather than additive linear effects.

alternatives: GaussianNB may win if the sample is small, features are poorly scaled, or the RBF hyperparameters are unsuitable.
Any gain may come from margin maximization or kernel smoothing rather than true nonlinear class structure.
candidates.applicability: Applies when features are scaled and the fixed split has a smooth nonlinear boundary; may be sensitive to C, gamma, and feature scaling.
falsification: SVC accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split.
SVC accuracy fails to exceed GaussianNB even when the fixed split contains a smooth nonlinear boundary.
candidates.mechanism: RBF-kernel SVC with C=2.0 maps features into an implicit high-dimensional space and fits a maximum-margin nonlinear decision boundary, allowing smooth curved class separation.
predictions: On the fixed public split, svc_rbf with C=2.0 will achieve higher diagnostic label accuracy than GaussianNB.
The improvement will be greater when classes are not linearly separable but are separable by a smooth nonlinear boundary.

alternatives: GaussianNB may outperform extra trees if the dataset is small, noisy, or the random split thresholds discard useful signal.
Any gain may be due to ensemble variance reduction rather than nonlinear interaction modeling.
candidates.applicability: Applies when the fixed split has nonlinear interactions or threshold effects; depth 8 may underfit very complex boundaries or overfit noisy small data.
falsification: Extra trees accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split.
Extra trees accuracy fails to exceed GaussianNB even when nonlinear interactions are present in the fixed split.
candidates.mechanism: Extremely randomized trees average 200 depth-8 trees with random split thresholds, increasing randomization and reducing variance while capturing nonlinear feature interactions.
predictions: On the fixed public split, extra_trees with max_depth=8 and n_estimators=200 will achieve higher diagnostic label accuracy than GaussianNB.
The improvement will be larger when nonlinear interactions are present and the dataset is not dominated by conditional independence.

alternatives: GaussianNB may match or exceed logistic regression if the Gaussian and conditional independence assumptions hold well on this dataset.
Any observed improvement may come from regularization or preprocessing rather than the discriminative linear mechanism.
candidates.applicability: Applies when features are numeric or encoded and the fixed public split has enough samples per class to estimate linear coefficients; performance may degrade if the true decision boundary is strongly nonlinear.
falsification: Logistic regression accuracy is less than or equal to GaussianNB accuracy on the fixed split.
The accuracy gap is negative under repeated resampling of the same fixed split if the split is the only source of variation.
candidates.mechanism: L2-regularized logistic regression learns a discriminative linear decision boundary in the original feature space, directly optimizing conditional likelihood without assuming feature independence or Gaussian class-conditionals.
predictions: On the fixed public split, logistic_regression with C=1.0 will achieve higher diagnostic label accuracy than the GaussianNB baseline.
The accuracy gap will be non-negative and, if present, will tend to be larger when features are correlated or class-conditional distributions are non-Gaussian.

decisions.rationale: 先执行预注册基线，建立方向统一效应的控制值。

The registered frozen configuration is {"model": "logistic_regression", "C": 1.0}, but the entrypoint's estimator() only constructed GaussianNB and raised NotImplementedError for every other candidate, so the hypothesis (L2-regularized logistic regression versus the GaussianNB baseline on the fixed public split) was never actually executed. This edit adds an executable branch in estimator() that is reached on every prediction run: it checks the frozen model name and returns sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=1.0) fitted on the original, unscaled feature space, matching the stated mechanism (discriminative linear boundary, conditional likelihood, no Gaussian/independence assumption) and the frozen config (only model and C are consumed; no new hyperparameters, no scaling, no resampling, no change to the split). max_iter is raised so the deterministic default lbfgs solver converges on unscaled features and the run reliably produces predictions. The raise remains as the guard for unregistered candidates. The existing gaussian_nb branch is left byte-identical so the baseline and the comparison remain intact, and the argparse CLI contract (--train, --input, --output, --config, --seed), the JSON input/output schema, and the train-only fitting path are unchanged. No test labels, network, secrets, or out-of-directory files are touched; prediction reads only the provided train/input/config files. prepare_data.py is left untouched because the frozen public split and its provenance are part of the fixed scientific configuration.
